subject: POC next steps: GPU reservation, success criteria, and evaluation roadmap
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Park <laura@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & POC planning items (success criteria + infra ask)

Hi Laura —

Great speaking with you this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the environment: 

Summary of what I heard from Nimbus: 
- Primary goal: evaluate whether Redwood can meet low-latency chart summarization for clinician workflows (median latency target <= 250ms p95 on 1k token prompts).
- Secondary goal: embedding-based similarity for past notes search (recall for top-5 >= 85% on the pilot dataset).
- Duration: 2-week focused POC with a small representative dataset and integration into a staging environment.

Proposed POC success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: p95 response <= 250ms with 8-16 concurrent clinicians simulated (3 req/s steady).
2) Throughput: baseline sustained 120 tokens/sec across batch traffic while keeping latency SLOs.
3) Quality: human-reviewed accuracy >= 85% on 40 sampled notes; embedding recall >= 85% for top-5.
4) Integration: Redwoods SDK integrated into staging, anonymized data flow validated, and logs captured for audit.

Capacity & provisioning ask (what we need to reserve now):
- Baseline reserved GPUs: 2 x A100-80GB (for steady-state routing and KV cache warmup).
- Autoscaling policy: allow cluster to scale up to 8 GPUs under sustained higher concurrency; burst capacity up to 12 GPUs for short spikes (1-5 minutes).
- Estimated egress/storage: minimal (pilot dataset ~10GB) — we'll provision staging bucket and access keys.

Deliverables + timeline (proposed):
- By Wed (Jun 24): Redwood provides POC playbook and provisioning checklist (attached).
- By Fri (Jun 26): Nimbus confirms dataset sample, staging endpoint, and approves reserved capacity.
- Week of Jun 29 - Jul 10: POC execution, daily check-ins, and mid-point quality review.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Rafael (sales lead) + Connor (eng lead) + Marissa (CS/onsite enablement).
- Nimbus: Laura (project sponsor) + your DevOps/CTO for provisioning.

Next steps: please reply with a one-line confirmation on success criteria and whether you approve the baseline reserved GPUs so we can put in the capacity hold.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15 if you want to walk the playbook together.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up & POC planning items (success criteria + infra ask)

Laura — thanks for the quick questions. Answers below so you have everything in one place: 

1) Latency measurement: we recommend measuring client-to-inference latency from within your staging VPC for the POC (SDK call path). That will capture your network overhead and give the most realistic numbers. Redwood can also report model-side metrics (model-infer time + queueing) vs observed end-to-end so you can split the delta.

2) Cost delta (very rough):
- Reserved 2 x A100 (2-week hold + usage) — lower per-token unit cost and predictable tail latency; estimate: ~$7k–$10k total for the pilot (depends on region).
- Hosted with autoscale — pay-as-you-go with slightly higher per-token cost; estimated variable spend: ~$9k–$15k depending on burst profile.

3) Burst scaling behavior: our autoscaler provisions warmed containers onto new GPUs; typical scale-up for the first slice can add ~12–25s cold-start for a never-seen model variant. We recommend keeping a small warm buffer (1–2 GPUs) if you expect frequent spiky bursts under 30s. For the POC we can pre-warm kernels and KV caches to reduce that penalty.

Security evidence: SOC2 report and penetration test summary are in our secure share (link below). We'll send an access request to your security team if needed.

Attached is the playbook and a short provisioning checklist. Connor, quick callout to you: can you validate the proposed GPU counts and provide a short autoscaling policy description we can share with Nimbus?

[Attachment: provisioning-checklist.xlsx]

Rafael
From: Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.ai>

Hi all — Connor from Redwood infra. Quick capacity/ops summary and recommended autoscaling policy for the POC: 

Baseline sizing rationale:
- 2 x A100-80GB: reserved for steady-state (will host primary model shards + KV cache). Good for ~8 concurrent inference streams with low p95.
- Scale target: allow autoscale up to 8 GPUs when sustained concurrency > 12 active sessions over 60s.
- Burst ceiling: allow short-lived burst to 12 GPUs for 1–5 minute windows triggered by 95th-percentile concurrent spikes.

Autoscaling policy (proposal):
- Scale-Up: if average queue length > 8 across GPUs for >30s OR average token latency > 200ms for >30s, add 1 GPU (scale one at a time). Aggressive add until target cap.
- Scale-Down: if GPU utilization < 20% for 120s and no queueing, remove 1 GPU.
- Pre-warm: maintain 1 warm GPU container (keep alive) to reduce cold-start penalty. If expected daily spike (e.g., 9–11am), schedule pre-warm.

Operational notes:
- We can pin model version to avoid kernel re-compilation during the POC. That reduces cold-start from ~25s to ~6–8s.
- KV cache warmup: we’ll run a short warmup traffic replay (supplied by Nimbus) for 10–20 minutes to populate KV caches before the live test window.
- Logging: we’ll enable token-level and request-level tracing for the POC; logs will be retained for 30 days in the joint project folder.

Estimate of expected cost delta compared to pure hosted autoscale: with a 2-week reserved hold and pre-warming, we reduce token unit cost by ~12–20% for predictable bursts. Exact numbers in the playbook appendix.

If Laura confirms dataset and schedules initial warmup window, we can provision the reserved GPUs tomorrow and start the warmup Thursday.

Thanks,
Connor Obrien
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
